### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

> "the purchase order for more hours went across to the office yesterday afternoon, and he wants
> the desk to put the prepaid hours on the account now, priced and credited, so the queued work can
> be dispatched against them rather than billed at the walk-up rate."

> "He is content for the desk to do whatever it has to do on its own side of the account to get
> that done, and says so if he is told there is something to settle first; the purchase itself,
> though, is his to make, and he says he would rather run it himself than have someone put a number
> through on his behalf, so he will take it on when it is handed to him."

- **Target object**: a block of prepaid technician hours on the demand service rate program.
- **Timing**: now, at the frozen moment.
- **Boundary**: desk-side postings pre-authorised; the purchase itself reserved to him.
- **Authorisation mode**: the purchase is an owner act, handed over and run by the user.

The simulator is passive: name and company unprompted; on challenge the account number 620398 and
tax_id_last4 2247; it answers what it is asked (Halsted Exchange, CRAC-2, a maintenance agreement
at the pavilion, a purchase order number required on invoices) and refuses every figure ("he does
not know how many prepaid hours are left … he does not know what the account owes either, and will
not put a figure on it when pressed"). It waits: "Until the hours are priced or the purchase is
handed to him he waits: he does not push, he does not ask what else the desk might need to do". No
figure and no next step is leaked.

Program figures for the Critical Facility Response Program: published credit limit 75000, payment
term 45 days, suspension period 30 days, term 24 calendar months (*Fees, Credit Ceilings and
Payment Terms*; *The Window a Ceiling Review Reads*); block hour rate 120, minimum purchase 60,
expiry 18 months, rollover Yes (*Prepaid Hour Block Terms by Program*).

**(a) The reviewed open balance ceiling.** *Working Out the Open Balance Ceiling at Review*.

- *Window.* Baseline: the last 12 months. *The Window a Ceiling Review Reads*: the program has run
  less than a full term (9 months and a part of a tenth since 2025-12-01, against a term of 24
  months) and privileges have not been restored during it (`reinstatement_date` is empty) → "the
  record is read from the day the current term started, counting each month or part month up to the
  day of the review" → **2025-12-01 to 2026-09-18**.
- *Starting ceiling.* Baseline: the published credit limit 75000. *The Starting Ceiling a Review
  Works From*: the charges that fell due in that window are 9800 + 7200 + 1680 + 4230 + 7200 +
  4940 + 4750 = **39800**, which is above half the published credit limit (37500) but not above it
  → "that invoiced total rounded up to the next whole multiple of 1000 US dollars" = **40000**.
- *Payment record step.* Baseline: none. *Step for the Account's Payment Record at Review*:
  payments received in the window number **8** (2025-12-20 through 2026-08-20) and the most recent
  invoice to fall due (due 2026-09-06) has stood 12 days past its due day, no longer than the
  suspension period of 30 → **0.15**.
- *Arrears cut.* Baseline: nothing. *Cut for Arrears at a Ceiling Review*: Term 1 fails (12 days is
  not longer than 30). Term 2 holds — the most recent invoice to fall due stands past its due day,
  seven invoices fell due in the window (two or more), and the payments received in it (9800 + 7200
  + 1680 + 4230 + 3600 + 3600 + 2500 + 2440 = 35050) do not clear what it invoiced (39800), the
  open position of 4750 standing at or below the credit limit of 75000 → **0.10 taken off**.
- *Portfolio step.* Baseline: none. *Step for the Owner's Maintenance Portfolio at Review*: an
  active preventive maintenance agreement stands, its annual price 38400 is at or above 20000, and
  the installments that fell due on it in the last 12 months (4 × 9600 = 38400) are cleared by the
  payments received on it (4 × 9600 = 38400) → **0.12**.
- *Volume allowance.* Baseline: none. *Allowance for the Account's Call Volume at Review*: calls
  dispatched within the window read number **7** (2026-01-08, 2026-03-23, 2026-05-29, 2026-07-20,
  2026-08-12, 2026-09-03, 2026-09-15) and emergency dispatches counted in it number 2; the 6-to-11
  row governs whatever the emergency count → **7500 US dollars**.
- Assembly per the document's own order of the assembly — one combined factor, the allowance added
  afterwards, only the total rounded: 40000 × (1 + 0.15 + 0.12 − 0.10) = 40000 × 1.17 = 46800;
  + 7500 → **the ceiling written on the program = 54300.00**.

**(b) The price of the block.** *Working Out the Price of a Prepaid Hour Block*.

- *Window the drawing record is read over.* Baseline: the last 12 months. *The Window a Block
  Purchase Reads Drawn Hours Over*: the tier lets unused hours roll into the next program year and
  the program has run less than a full term → "the hours drawn are read over the tier's block
  expiry period" = **18 calendar months**, i.e. 2025-03-18 to 2026-09-18.
- *Prepaid hours standing and the shortfall.* Blocks bought within the tier's expiry period: the
  2024-12-10 block expired 2026-06-10, so 60 + 60 + 60 = **180** hours stand. Hours drawn over the
  window read: 38.0 + 41.5 + 35.5 + 44.0 + 52.5 + 48.0 + 57.0 + 61.5 + 55.0 + 37.0 = **470.0**.
  Prepaid hours standing = max(180 − 470, 0) = **0**; shortfall = 470 − 0 = **470.0 hours**.
- *Multiples sold.* Baseline: "sold as a single one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples, that
  is 1 multiple". *How Large a Prepaid Block the Drawing Record Calls For*: the shortfall of 470
  stands above one minimum purchase of 60 → "as many whole multiples as it takes to cover it,
  rounded up" = **8 multiples**. Hours sold = 8 × 60 = **480.0**.
- *Rate basis.* Baseline: the whole block at the tier's block hour rate. *Pricing a Block Multiple
  by Multiple*, Basis 1: the multiples sold stand at or above 4 and unexpired blocks already stand
  on the program → the first multiple at the block hour rate, each further multiple at the rate the
  block steps to. *The Rate a Larger Prepaid Block Steps To*: the multiples sold stand at or above
  2 and the owner holds an active preventive maintenance agreement → 120 × 0.94 = **112.80**.
  Block price = 60 × 120 + 420 × 112.80 = 7200 + 47376 = **54576.00**.
- *Discount.* Baseline: none. *Discount a Settlement Record Carries on a Block Purchase*: over the
  12 months to the day of the purchase the program invoiced 5800 + 9800 + 7200 + 1680 + 4230 +
  7200 + 4940 + 4750 = 45600 and received 22000 + 5800 + 9800 + 7200 + 1680 + 4230 + 3600 + 3600 +
  2500 + 2440 = 62850, so the payments cover what was invoiced; the open position, read over the
  whole life (67600 invoiced less 62850 received) is **4750** and therefore stands → **1.0 percent**
  = 545.76.
- *Headroom and office release charge.* The open position is 4750; the credit ceiling standing on
  the rate program, once (a) is written, is 54300, so the headroom is **49550** and the excess is
  54576 − 49550 = **5026.00**. Baseline: no office release charge. *Office Release Charge on a
  Block Bought Past the Ceiling*: the block price carries the open position past that ceiling and
  the most recent invoice to fall due (due 2026-09-06) stands past its due day → **3.0 percent on
  the excess** = 150.78.
- Assembly: block price less the discount worked out on the block price alone, with the office
  release charge added afterwards, only the total rounded half up: 54576.00 − 545.76 + 150.78 =
  **54181.02**.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer asked for exactly one thing: put the prepaid hours on the account, priced and
credited. The tree:

```
buy the block of prepaid hours               (root — the customer's own write, user-owned)
└── write a reviewed open balance ceiling on the rate program   (state-derived hop)
```

Handling order: ceiling review → block purchase.

**Hop 1 — the root waits on a ceiling change dated in the current program year. state-derived.**
The blocked policy's own hub, *Buying a Block of Prepaid Technician Hours*, states:

> "A block of prepaid hours is priced only once the credit ceiling standing on the rate program
> carries a change dated in the current program year. The current program year runs from the day
> the current term started to the day of the purchase."

The sentence names a **state** of the program record — that the ceiling standing on it carries a
change dated inside the current program year — and names no action, no tool and no other problem.
Checking the record: `find_service_programs` returns `last_change_type: 'primary_site_changed'`
and `last_change_date: '2025-06-18'`, while `term_start_date` is 2025-12-01. So the program's most
recent change is not a credit-ceiling change at all, and it is dated before the current term began:
the state does not hold on either count.

Searching the corpus in the words the record and the sentence use for that state — "credit
ceiling", "open balance ceiling", "rate program", "change" — reaches *Writing a Reviewed Open
Balance Ceiling on a Rate Program*, which describes the write that brings the state about:
"Exactly one term of the live program changes: the ceiling above which further work on the account
waits for an office release is replaced by the figure given, the program is stamped as having had
its credit ceiling changed, and the day of the change is recorded." That the review is genuinely
open is visible in the same document's opening: "Where that ceiling falls due for review, a
reviewed ceiling is written onto the live program in its place." The hop was mine to draw: the
purchase hub names no tool of that problem and no route.

No hop was **pre-solved**, and the tree is not aggregated anywhere: no document lists the two
problems together, and no sentence outside the purchase hub's own rule states the order.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure rests on a quoted sentence plus a returned row.

**Closest alternatives, each excluded by a visible sentence or record:**

| Alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Sell one multiple (60 hours), the hub's plain reading | *How Large a Prepaid Block the Drawing Record Calls For* rules the number of multiples off the shortfall, and 470 stands above one minimum purchase of 60. |
| Take `block_hours_remaining: 24.0` as the prepaid hours standing | The computation document defines them — "the hours of every block bought within the tier's expiry period less the hours drawn over the window read, never below nil" — and the caller disclaims the stored figure ("the portal has been showing the same figure for weeks and he stopped believing it"). A policy-side note, not a document defect. |
| Read hours drawn over 12 months | *The Window a Block Purchase Reads Drawn Hours Over* fixes the window at the tier's block expiry period for a rolling-over tier inside its term. |
| Price the whole block at the block hour rate (120) | *Pricing a Block Multiple by Multiple* Basis 1 applies because 8 ≥ 4 and unexpired blocks stand; only the first multiple takes 120. |
| Take the 2.0 percent settlement discount | *Discount a Settlement Record Carries on a Block Purchase* requires that no open position stands; the whole-life open position is 4750. |
| Measure the headroom against the published credit limit of 75000 | The computation document says "the credit ceiling is the one standing on the rate program", and after the review that is 54300. The published limit is what the **review** starts from, not what the purchase measures against. |
| Apply the office release charge before the discount | "the discount … is worked out on the block price alone and never on the price after the office release charge is added, with the office release charge added afterwards". |
| Use the last 12 months as the ceiling review window | *The Window a Ceiling Review Reads* shortens it to the term start where the program has run less than a full term and privileges were not restored. |
| The agent runs the purchase | "the purchase itself, though, is his to make"; the hub: "This is the building owner's own act." |
| The 2025-11-03 enrollment or the 2025-06-18 primary-site change satisfies the prerequisite | The sentence requires a change **to the credit ceiling standing on the rate program**, dated in the current program year; `last_change_type` is `primary_site_changed` and its date precedes the term start. |

**Against "do only the one thing the customer asked for".** Pricing and handing over the purchase
without the ceiling review is excluded by reasoning from the visible rule, not by any route: the
purchase hub's own sentence makes the price underivable — "A block of prepaid hours is priced only
once the credit ceiling standing on the rate program carries a change dated in the current program
year" — and the program record shows no such change. It is also excluded arithmetically: the
headroom, and with it the excess and the office release charge, are measured against "the credit
ceiling standing on the rate program", which is 75000 before the review and 54300 after. Doing only
the one thing yields 54576.00 − 545.76 + 0 = 54030.24 instead of 54181.02, and leaves the program
carrying a ceiling that the review's own rule says falls due to be replaced.

| block price | 1 multiple × 60 h × 120 = 7200, no discount, headroom 70250 leaves no excess → **7200.00** | 54181.02 (480.0 hours) |

### Checks specific to this step

- **The hop was not pre-solved.** The edge's `resolved_by` (`set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3`)
  and `condition` are authoring fields and appear nowhere in the corpus; the purchase hub names only
  its own tool. The blind audit found the ceiling-review document by searching the state's own words
  ("credit ceiling", "change", "rate program") and by reading `last_change_type` /
  `last_change_date` off the program record — which is exactly the evidence the source's
  `unresolved_at_frozen_time` block cites.
- **No conclusion rested on hidden compute.** Every intermediate (10-month window, 39800 invoiced,
  40000 starting ceiling, 8 payments, 7 invoices, 35050 received, 38400 agreement price, 7 calls,
  470 shortfall, 8 multiples, 112.80 stepped rate, 4750 open position, 49550 headroom, 5026 excess)
  appears in the source's `factor_trace` with the same tier and the same figure.
- **Tool schemas agree with the source solution**, and both calls returned the receipts the
  documents describe.
- **Every declared factor is entailed and reachable.** All twelve factors of the two computations
  were found from the customer's records during the blind phase, none by guessing.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME PASS.** From the runtime-visible materials alone the branch was derived, the problem
tree the customer never mentioned was reconstructed, and both scored figures, the hours sold and the
tool sequence equal the source layer's.
